lessons.title: Let's Meet Up!

items.example: Quand est-ce que tu es libre ?
items.exampleMeaning: When are you free?
I am going to the cinema on Saturday.

items.example: Où se retrouver pour le café ?
items.exampleMeaning: Where shall we meet for coffee?
I want to invite my friends.

items.example: C'est une bonne idée d'aller au parc.
items.exampleMeaning: It's a good idea to go to the park.
Can you come on Saturday?

lessons.tip: Use 'Quand ?' to ask about time, and 'À quelle heure ?' for specific times. Remember to use the correct day in your plans.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quand est-ce que tu es libre ?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: At what time do we start?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'est une bonne idée d'aller au parc !
dialogue.meaning: It's a good idea to go to the park!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: I want to invite my friends.

scenario.partnerRole: A is a friend making plans.
scenario.learnerRole: You are the person responding to the invitation.
scenario.brief: Ask about availability and suggest a time to meet. Use the new words from this lesson.
scenario.goal: You will confirm your availability for Saturday.

lessons.title: Setting a Date

items.exampleMeaning: We have an appointment on Sunday.
On Monday, I cannot.
The appointment is at 10 o'clock.

items.example: Dimanche à 10 heures, est-ce que ça te va ?
items.exampleMeaning: Sunday at 10 o'clock, does that work for you?
I prefer Monday.
Okay, it's noted for Sunday.

lessons.tip: Use 'D'accord' to agree with a plan. If you have a preference, say 'Je préfère...' to express it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: We have an appointment on Sunday.

scenario.partnerRole: A is confirming the date and time.
scenario.learnerRole: You are responding to the confirmation.
scenario.brief: Discuss the appointment and express your preferences.
scenario.goal: You will agree on the date and time.

lessons.title: Making Invitations

items.exampleMeaning: I invite you to my party.
I accept the invitation.
I decline the invitation.
Can you come to my party?

items.example: Je suis content, ça me fait plaisir !
items.exampleMeaning: I am happy, that makes me happy!

items.example: Merci pour l'invitation à ta fête.
items.exampleMeaning: Thank you for the invitation to your party.

lessons.tip: Use 'Je t'invite à...' to make an invitation. If you accept, say 'J'accepte', and if you decline, say 'Je refuse'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: I invite you to my party.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je suis content, ça me fait plaisir !
dialogue.meaning: I am happy, that makes me happy!

scenario.partnerRole: A is inviting you to a party.
scenario.learnerRole: You are responding to the invitation.
scenario.brief: Make an invitation and respond to it.

lessons.title: Confirming Plans

items.example: C'est bon pour moi, je viendrai.
items.exampleMeaning: It's good for me, I will come.
We see each other on Sunday?
Call me back tomorrow.

items.example: Je vais vérifier mon emploi du temps.
items.exampleMeaning: I will check my schedule.

items.example: Tout est prêt pour la fête ?
items.exampleMeaning: Is everything ready for the party?

items.example: C'est confirmé, nous avons un rendez-vous à 15 heures.
items.exampleMeaning: It's confirmed, we have an appointment at 3 PM.

lessons.tip: Use 'C'est bon pour moi' to confirm plans. You can also ask 'Tout est prêt ?' to check on preparations.
